correctness.rationale: For 1<=m<=n, at a zero entry f_ij the Italian defense inequality is precisely row_sum_i+column_sum_j>=2. If a row has weight zero, all columns have >=2; if a row has weight one, all columns are positive; if every row has weight >=2, total >=2m. This proves weight >=min(n,2m); a surjection assigning one 1 to each column with each row occupied attains n, and arbitrary weight-two rows attain 2m. Equality excludes zero rows and yields either the one-1-per-column onto family or independent weight-two rows. Counts are m!S(n,m), [n+binom(n,2)]^m, and at n=2m inclusion–exclusion subtracts n!/(2!)^m. Degenerate R_1,1 is correctly a single 1. Independent literal-rook-neighborhood enumeration of all 3^(mn) labelings at sizes (1,1),(1,2),(1,3),(2,2),(2,3),(2,4),(3,3) reproduced gamma and counts including (2,4)=(4,108).
